title: Complete-base projectivity from integral fibres and projective reduction
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and assume $A$ is $I$-adically complete. Let $A\to B$ be a finite type flat homomorphism of commutative rings. For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, suppose the fibre $F_{\mathfrak p}=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a nonzero integral domain (that is, $1\ne0$ and $xy=0$ implies $x=0$ or $y=0$). If $B/IB$ is projective over $A/I$, then $B$ is projective over $A$. The notions of Noetherian, completeness, finite type, flatness, tensor product, residue field and projectivity are as in [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], [def-weil-residue-field] and [def-weil-pbc-projective-module].

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ and write $j_{\mathfrak p}:B\to F_{\mathfrak p}$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $A/\mathfrak p\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is injective: an element $a/1$ in $\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ has $sa\in\mathfrak p$ for some $s\notin\mathfrak p$, after taking common denominators, so $a\in\mathfrak p$. Tensor this injection with the flat $A$-module $B$, using exactly the injection-preserving definition [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. The tensor relations [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] give inverse maps $(A/\mathfrak p)\otimes_AB\rightleftarrows B/\mathfrak pB$, $\bar a\otimes b\mapsto ab\bmod\mathfrak pB$ and $\bar b\mapsto\bar1\otimes b$: the second kills $\mathfrak pB$ since $\bar1\otimes ab=\bar a\otimes b=0$ for $a\in\mathfrak p$, and the composites fix generators. Likewise the tensor flip sends $\lambda\otimes b$ to $b\otimes\lambda$, with itself as inverse. Under these maps the tensor injection is $B/\mathfrak pB\to F_{\mathfrak p}$ induced by $j_{\mathfrak p}$. Hence $\ker j_{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak pB$.

source.place: Tag 05FS, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective, final paragraph, specialized to the already complete base; elementary tensor and annihilator calculations expanded.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q$ be an associated prime of $F_{\mathfrak p}$ as a $B$-module. By [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes], there is $z\in F_{\mathfrak p}$ with $\mathfrak q=\{b:j_{\mathfrak p}(b)z=0\}$. Since $\mathfrak q$ is proper, $z\ne0$. The assumed domain property of $F_{\mathfrak p}$ gives $j_{\mathfrak p}(b)z=0$ if and only if $j_{\mathfrak p}(b)=0$. Step 1 therefore gives $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak pB$. This computes the associated primes as $B$-module annihilators directly; no change-of-ring assertion for associated primes is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 05FS, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective, final paragraph, specialized to the already complete base; elementary tensor and annihilator calculations expanded.

proof.text: Completeness and [lem-weil-pbc-adic-complete-jacobson-radical] imply that the nonempty closed set $V(\mathfrak p)$ meets $V(I)$; it is nonempty since it contains $\mathfrak p$. Thus choose a prime $\mathfrak r\supseteq\mathfrak p+I$. The canonical unital map $j_{\mathfrak r}:B\to B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ kills both $\mathfrak pB$ and $IB$: for $a\in\mathfrak r$ and $b\in B$, $j_{\mathfrak r}(ab)=b\otimes\bar a=0$, by the residue-field and tensor descriptions [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The target is nonzero by hypothesis. Consequently $IB+\mathfrak pB\ne B$, since otherwise this map would kill $1$. By step 2 this proves $IB+\mathfrak q\ne B$ for every associated prime required by the complete-base projectivity criterion.

source.place: Tag 05FS, final two sentences, with Algebra Tag 05GI, lemma-radical-completion (4). The nonempty-fibre argument is expanded by the canonical unital map.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-local-flat-pure-complete-projective] with its $(A,I,B,M)$ equal to $(A,I,B,B)$. The module $B$ is finite over itself, generated by $1$. Its flatness over $A$, finite type of $A\to B$, Noetherianity and completeness of $A$, and projectivity of $B/IB$ over $A/I$ are the stated hypotheses. Steps 2--3 give its associated-prime condition for every $\mathfrak p$ and every associated $\mathfrak q$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$. The criterion concludes that $B$ is projective over $A$.
